This lesson turns that one sentence into four visible things at four stations.

四个站位 · 一张实验台 · 全程不换场景: Four stations · one bench · no scene changes throughout
刚切开的钠亮得发光，为什么十几秒就暗了？: Freshly cut sodium is dazzlingly shiny, so why does it dull within seconds?
把「在空气中放置的时间」从 0 拖到 60 s 以上，盯住玻璃片上钠块的切面: Drag "Time exposed to air" from 0 to beyond 60 s and watch the cut surface of the sodium on the glass plate
敞口放置：0 s 银白色（0.0 mmol，光泽 100 %）→ 10 s 已变: Open to air: 0 s silvery white (0.0 mmol, luster 100 %) → 10 s already dull (1.6 mmol, 81.9 %) → 60 s whole piece dull (6.1 mmol, 30.1 %) → 300 s (8.7 mmol, 0.2 %); the piece in the kerosene bottle stays silvery white
新切开的钠的光亮的表面很快变暗了，这是因为钠与氧气发生反应，在钠的表面生成了一薄: The shiny surface of freshly cut sodium soon dulls because sodium reacts with oxygen and forms a thin layer of oxide on its surface; this oxide is sodium oxide: 4Na + O₂ = 2Na₂O (textbook wording). So sodium spoiling in air is a redox reaction (answer to textbook p.43 Exercise 4).
A2.4、A2.6、A2.16、B2.4、B2.5、标准值表 2–4、D3: A2.4, A2.6, A2.16, B2.4, B2.5, reference table rows 2–4, D3
「变暗」不是脏了，是表面生成了一薄层 Na₂O。: "Dulling" isn't dirt; it's a thin layer of Na₂O forming on the surface.
光泽从 100 % 一路掉到 0.2 %，钠一直在失电子：0.0 → 8.7 m: Luster falls from 100 % to 0.2 % while sodium keeps losing electrons: 0.0 → 8.7 mmol.
曲线图上实线（敞口）掉得很快、虚线（泡在煤油里）几乎不动。: On the chart the solid line (open to air) drops fast while the dashed line (under kerosene) hardly moves.
去掉这一步：学生以为钠本来就是灰的，不知道「银白色」才是它本来的样子。: Skip this step and students think sodium is naturally gray, not knowing that silvery white is its true appearance.
高频：钠在空气中变暗的原因与方程式；判断是否属于氧化还原反应。: Frequently tested: why sodium dulls in air and the equation; whether it is a redox reaction.

那怎么才能让它不变暗？: So how do you stop it dulling?
把「保存在煤油中」打开，再看同样放 300 s 的钠块: Turn on "Stored in kerosene" and look at the sodium after the same 300 s
同样放 300 s：敞口 8.7 mmol、光泽只剩 0.2 %（整块变暗）→: After the same 300 s: open to air 8.7 mmol with only 0.2 % luster left (whole piece dull) → under kerosene 1.9 mmol with 78.7 % luster (still silvery white, just slightly dull); the dashed (kerosene) line on the chart is almost flat
教材 p.35：要把钠保存在石蜡油或煤油中，以隔绝空气。煤油把空气挡住，钠就接触: Textbook p.35: sodium is stored in paraffin oil or kerosene to keep air out. Kerosene blocks the air, so sodium can't reach O₂ and won't dull.
A2.6、A1.4、B2.4、标准值表 4–5、D1: A2.6, A1.4, B2.4, reference table rows 4–5, D1
挡住的是空气里的 O₂，不是钠本身——「隔绝空气」四个字就是煤油的全部作用。: What is blocked is the O₂ in air, not the sodium itself; "keeping air out" is the whole job of kerosene.
同样 300 s：敞口 8.7 mmol、煤油 1.9 mmol，差 4.6 倍: Same 300 s: open 8.7 mmol, kerosene 1.9 mmol, a 4.6× difference.

高频：钠的保存方法与原因（隔绝空气、防水）。: Frequently tested: how sodium is stored and why (keep out air and water).

把它加热，钠会变成什么？为什么不是氧化钠？: What does sodium turn into when heated, and why isn't it sodium oxide?
把「加热（酒精灯外焰）」打开，盯住坩埚里的钠从熔化到燃烧: Turn on "Heating (alcohol lamp outer flame)" and watch the sodium in the crucible go from melting to burning
常温 60 s：整块变暗（6.1 mmol，灰白，生成 Na₂O）→ 加热：先熔: Room temperature 60 s: whole piece dull (6.1 mmol, grayish white, Na₂O) → heated: first melts into a bead → yellow flame → pale-yellow solid (8.7 mmol, Na₂O₂); the room-temperature control beside it stays grayish white
钠受热后先熔化，然后与氧气剧烈反应，发出黄色火焰，生成一种淡黄色固体——过氧化钠: When heated, sodium first melts, then reacts violently with oxygen, giving a yellow flame and a pale-yellow solid, sodium peroxide: 2Na + O₂ =△= Na₂O₂ (textbook wording). Burning sodium forms Na₂O₂, not Na₂O (textbook p.43 Exercise 3 marks "burning sodium forms sodium oxide" as the wrong option).
A2.7、A2.15、A2.18、B2.1 算子 7/8、标准值表 6–7、D3: A2.7, A2.15, A2.18, B2.1 operators 7/8, reference table rows 6–7, D3
常温与加热是两种不同产物：Na₂O（灰白）与 Na₂O₂（淡黄）——颜色一变就是: Room temperature and heating give two different products: Na₂O (grayish white) and Na₂O₂ (pale yellow); the color change is the evidence.

钠的性质非常活泼，能与水发生剧烈反应；反应时放出热量；反应后得到的溶液显碱性（教: Sodium is very active and reacts violently with water; the reaction releases heat and the resulting solution is basic (textbook wording): 2Na + 2H₂O = 2NaOH + H₂↑. The red comes from the NaOH produced meeting phenolphthalein, not from sodium itself.

五个字各有依据：浮←密度 0.97 < 1.00；熔←放热、超过熔点 97.79: Each word has a reason: floats ← density 0.97 < 1.00; melts ← heat released, above the 97.79 ℃ melting point; darts · hisses ← H₂ gas produced; red ← the solution is basic (textbook p.36 only gives three angles: position / shape / solution color; the five words are a common teaching summary).
对照烧杯没滴酚酞：无色，但 pH 一样是 12.94——碱性是反应给的，酚酞只是: The control beaker has no phenolphthalein: colorless, but pH still 12.94; the basicity comes from the reaction, phenolphthalein only shows it.
不要近距离俯视烧杯（教材 p.36 的注意框）。: Don't look down into the beaker from close up (warning box, textbook p.36).
